title: Insurance Reimbursement Estimator
problem: Chiropractors spend significant time estimating expected insurance reimbursements for different CPT codes and payers. Incorrect estimates lead to cash flow surprises and difficulty setting patient financial expectations. Underbilling or overbilling can trigger audits or lost revenue.
who: Solo practitioners and small group practice owners managing their own billing

skill_spec.name: Chiropractic Reimbursement Estimator
skill_spec.one_liner: Calculates expected insurance reimbursement for chiropractic CPT codes by payer type and region.

inputs.name: payer_type
inputs.label: Payer type (Medicare, Medicaid, BCBS, Aetna, UHC, Cigna, Cash)

skill_spec.formula_hint: Base Medicare rate by CPT code * geographic adjustment factor (GPCI). Commercial payers typically 110-150% of Medicare rates. Apply modifier adjustments for 25, 59, etc.

example_queries: How much will Medicare reimburse for 98941 in California?
Estimate my monthly revenue for 80 visits with a mix of BCBS and UHC patients using 98940 and 98941
What's the typical reimbursement difference between Medicare and Aetna for a CMT visit?

title: SOAP Note Generator
problem: Chiropractors must complete SOAP notes for every patient encounter, often 20-30 per day. Same-day documentation is required for compliance, but writing detailed notes is time-consuming and repetitive. Incomplete or vague SOAP notes lead to claim denials and audit failures.
who: All practicing chiropractors, especially high-volume solo practitioners

skill_spec.name: Chiropractic SOAP Note Generator
skill_spec.one_liner: Generates compliant, detailed SOAP notes from brief clinical inputs for chiropractic visits.

variables.name: region_treated
variables.label: Spinal region(s) treated (cervical, thoracic, lumbar, sacral)

skill_spec.structure_hint: S: Patient reported [complaint], pain [scale]/10, aggravating/relieving factors -> O: ROM [findings], palpation findings, orthopedic tests, adjustment performed [technique] to [regions] -> A: [diagnosis] improving/stable/worsening, functional progress -> P: Continue [frequency], reassess in [timeframe], home exercises [list]

example_queries: Write a SOAP note for a lumbar adjustment using diversified technique, patient reports 6/10 low back pain radiating to left leg
Generate a progress note for cervical and thoracic adjustment, patient improving from MVA, pain down from 8 to 4
Create a SOAP note for a new patient with chronic neck pain, restricted ROM, treated with Activator method

title: Insurance Claim Denial Resolution Checklist
problem: Chiropractic claims have high denial rates, especially from Medicare and managed care. Each denied claim requires investigation, appeal preparation, and resubmission. Many chiropractors write off denied claims rather than appeal, losing thousands in legitimate revenue.
who: Solo practitioners and billing staff in chiropractic offices

skill_spec.name: Chiropractic Claim Denial Resolution
skill_spec.one_liner: Step-by-step process to identify denial reason, prepare documentation, and file appeals for denied chiropractic insurance claims.
steps: Step 1: Identify denial reason code from ERA/EOB (CO-4, CO-11, CO-16, CO-50, CO-97, PR-1, etc.)
Step 2: Verify patient eligibility and benefits were active on date of service
Step 3: Check CPT-ICD code pairing - ensure diagnosis supports medical necessity for CMT
Step 4: Review SOAP note for date of service - confirm documentation supports codes billed
Step 5: Check if prior authorization was required and obtained
Step 6: Verify timely filing - check payer-specific deadline (typically 90-365 days)
Step 7: For medical necessity denials - prepare Letter of Medical Necessity with clinical rationale
Step 8: Gather supporting documentation (X-rays, ROM measurements, functional outcome scores)
Step 9: Submit corrected claim or formal appeal with cover letter within appeal deadline
Step 10: Track appeal status - follow up at 30/60/90 days
Step 11: If appeal denied, consider external review or state insurance commissioner complaint
warnings: Warning: Medicare appeals have strict 120-day deadline from date of initial determination
Warning: Do not rebill denied claims as new claims - this can be flagged as duplicate billing fraud
Warning: Document all phone calls with payer (date, time, rep name, reference number)
regulatory_refs: State insurance regulations for commercial appeal rights

example_queries: My 98941 claim was denied with code CO-16, what do I do?
How do I appeal a Medicare denial for medical necessity on chiropractic care?
Step by step - how to handle a claim denied for no prior authorization?

title: Treatment Plan Generator
problem: Creating individualized treatment plans with proper frequency, duration, and measurable goals is required by insurers for reimbursement. Poorly written plans trigger audits and denials. Chiropractors rewrite similar plans repeatedly with minor variations.
who: All practicing chiropractors, especially those dealing with PI and WC cases

skill_spec.name: Chiropractic Treatment Plan Generator
skill_spec.one_liner: Generates insurance-compliant treatment plans with measurable goals, visit frequency, and duration based on diagnosis and clinical findings.

variables.name: onset_type
variables.label: Onset type (acute, subacute, chronic, MVA, work injury)

skill_spec.structure_hint: Patient demographics -> Diagnosis and clinical findings -> Treatment goals (measurable: pain reduction, ROM improvement, functional milestones) -> Treatment frequency and duration (Phase 1: acute 3x/week x 4 weeks, Phase 2: corrective 2x/week x 6 weeks, Phase 3: maintenance 1x/month) -> Modalities and techniques per visit -> Re-evaluation schedule -> Discharge criteria

example_queries: Create a treatment plan for acute lumbar disc herniation, 45-year-old, pain 8/10, 40% ROM loss
Generate a PI treatment plan for a 32-year-old MVA patient with cervical whiplash
Write a treatment plan for chronic low back pain patient transitioning to maintenance care

title: Practice Revenue and Overhead Calculator
problem: Most chiropractors are practice owners but lack business training. They struggle to calculate true profitability after overhead (rent, staff, supplies, malpractice insurance, student loans). Poor financial visibility leads to undercharging, overspending, or inability to scale.
who: Solo practitioners and small group practice owners

skill_spec.name: Chiropractic Practice Profitability Calculator
skill_spec.one_liner: Calculates practice profitability, overhead ratio, and per-visit profit based on revenue, expenses, and patient volume.
skill_spec.formula_hint: Gross revenue = visits * avg_collection. Total overhead = rent + payroll + supplies + (malpractice/12) + loan + other. Overhead ratio = overhead/revenue * 100. Net = revenue - overhead. Breakeven = overhead / avg_collection. Industry benchmark overhead ratio: 50-65%.

example_queries: I see 320 patients/month collecting $60 average, rent is $3500, one CA at $3200/mo - what's my profit?
Calculate my overhead ratio - I'm bringing in $22k/month with $13k in expenses
How many patients per month do I need to break even with $8,000 in fixed costs?

title: Medicare Compliance Checklist for Chiropractors
problem: Medicare covers only manual spinal subluxation correction (98940-98943) with strict documentation requirements. Chiropractors frequently get audited by Medicare and face recoupment demands. Non-compliant billing can result in exclusion from the Medicare program.
who: All chiropractors who accept Medicare patients

skill_spec.name: Medicare Chiropractic Compliance Checklist
skill_spec.one_liner: Ensures every Medicare chiropractic visit meets CMS documentation and billing requirements to prevent audit failures and recoupment.
steps: Step 1: Confirm subluxation is documented - must be identified by X-ray or physical exam (2 of 4 PART criteria: Pain/tenderness, Asymmetry, Range of motion abnormality, Tissue/tone changes)
Step 2: Verify only covered CPT codes billed to Medicare (98940, 98941, 98942, 98943 only)
Step 3: Ensure AT modifier is used for active/corrective treatment (not maintenance care)
Step 4: Document medical necessity - treatment must demonstrate expected functional improvement
Step 5: Verify SOAP note includes: specific subluxation level(s), treatment rendered, patient response
Step 6: Check that initial visit includes history, exam findings, and diagnosis with subluxation level
Step 7: Confirm treatment plan is on file with frequency, duration, and measurable goals
Step 8: Verify re-evaluation documented every 30 days or 12 visits (whichever comes first)
Step 9: Do NOT bill Medicare for maintenance care - must use ABN (Advance Beneficiary Notice) if continuing
Step 10: Ensure all modifiers correct: AT (active treatment), GA (ABN on file), GY (excluded service)
warnings: Warning: Medicare does NOT cover X-rays, exams, therapies, or modalities when billed by chiropractors - only CMT
Warning: Maintenance care billed as active treatment is the #1 cause of Medicare chiropractic audits
Warning: Failure to use AT modifier correctly can trigger 100% recoupment of claims

example_queries: What documentation does Medicare require for each chiropractic visit?
When do I need to use the AT modifier vs GA modifier for Medicare?
How do I properly transition a Medicare patient from active care to maintenance with an ABN?

title: Personal Injury Case Value Estimator
problem: PI (personal injury) and MVA (motor vehicle accident) cases are highly profitable for chiropractors but require careful documentation and billing strategy. Undervaluing cases means lost revenue; overbilling risks fraud allegations. Chiropractors need to estimate reasonable case values for attorney communications.

skill_spec.name: PI/MVA Case Value Estimator
skill_spec.one_liner: Estimates reasonable chiropractic treatment costs for personal injury cases based on injury type, treatment duration, and regional averages.

inputs.name: injury_type
inputs.label: Primary injury (cervical whiplash, lumbar sprain, disc herniation, multi-region)

outputs.name: typical_range
outputs.label: Typical case value range for this injury type (USD)

skill_spec.formula_hint: Total visits = weeks * frequency. CMT cost = visits * regional CMT rate ($50-150). Therapy = visits * modality rate ($30-80). Initial exam $150-350. X-ray $75-300. MRI referral $500-2500. Typical whiplash case: $3,000-$15,000. Disc herniation: $8,000-$30,000.

example_queries: Estimate total chiropractic cost for a moderate cervical whiplash, 12 weeks treatment at 3x/week
What's a reasonable case value for a lumbar disc herniation from MVA with 6 months of care?
How much should I expect to bill for a mild whiplash PI case in Florida?

title: Informed Consent Form Generator
problem: Informed consent is legally required before chiropractic treatment, especially for cervical manipulation. Each state has different requirements for what must be disclosed. Generic forms may not meet state-specific standards, creating liability exposure.
who: All practicing chiropractors, especially new practice owners
